clue.text: Edited words with a pen in book

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor reworks some lines written with a pen inside a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Adams's novel about a warren of rabbits is a famous example of a book.

clue.text: American aside, note a lot bowling changed footwear

indicators.note: put aside means the letter for American is set apart from the pool before it is reworked
changed says the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American remarks in an aside that cricket bowling changed a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aside' removes A from NOTEALOTBOWLING, and 'changed' rearranges the fourteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber knee-high boot is a kind of footwear, named after the Duke who popularised it.

clue.text: The Barnsley Chronicle's provocative online presence

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect, spoken in Barnsley, 'the' is shortened to t'
a roll is an official record or chronicle

explanation.surface: A local newspaper's website seems to be stirring up trouble online.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnsley is a Yorkshire town, where 'the' is famously clipped to t'; the Barnsley Chronicle is also a real local paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who posts inflammatory messages on the internet to provoke reactions is known by this name.

clue.text: Screen broadcast describing team's dwellings

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round means the shuffled letters encircle the next piece
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of screen are rearranged

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A screened broadcast portrays the homes belonging to a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Residences are homes or places where people live, plain synonyms for dwellings.

clue.text: Houses close to smallish fox burrows

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a fox's den is called an earth

explanation.surface: Some homes sit close to small burrows dug by foxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a verb but is a plural noun, figuratively standing for homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireside stands for the home itself, so these can mean households or houses.

clue.text: Rising regularly, cost not stopping party for US banker

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from bottom to top
stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party within a larger group

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Rising costs not stopping a political party is a worry for an American banker.
explanation.walkthrough: A river is a 'banker' because it has banks; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Washington DC is a US river, a crossword 'banker' since it has banks.

clue.text: Past secret discovered

indicators.note: discovered read as dis-covered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go; that the answer also sits inside this word is a coincidence

parts.note: covert means secret or hidden

explanation.surface: A long-hidden secret from the past has come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is read as 'uncovered': COVERT loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished or gone by, as in 'the danger is past', is the meaning shared.

clue.text: Careless in not discarding old short dressing-gown previously

indicators.note: previously says the clipped garment comes before the other piece
short means the last letter of the garment's name is cut off

parts.note: a negligee is a light dressing-gown

indicators.note: discarding means throwing away the letter that follows from the word not

explanation.surface: Someone was careless in not throwing out an old, short dressing-gown earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarding old' takes O from NOT to leave NT; 'short' cuts NEGLIGEE to NEGLIGE, which 'previously' places first. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking proper care or attention is a synonym for careless.

clue.text: Statement, indirectly, of what political journalist did?

definitions.meaning: an utterance relayed indirectly, as in 'he said that he would come'
a journalist covering politics wrote up and relayed a speech in the newspaper

explanation.surface: A political journalist's job is to relay what was said, indirectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the grammatical term into a verb and a noun: the journalist reported a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammar term for indirect statement, where words are relayed rather than quoted.

clue.text: Hurry up appearance by Sting

parts.note: a look is someone's appearance
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to hurry, because the singer Sting is about to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the singer misleads; here it is a verb meaning to hurt. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British imperative meaning be quick or get moving.

clue.text: Bore, keen to advance reputation primarily

indicators.note: to advance means a letter moves forward one place within the word

parts.note: eager means keen

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A dull person is keen to boost their standing above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives R, and 'to advance' moves the R of EAGER one place earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore, a wave surging up a river estuary, is also called by this rare name.

clue.text: Excluding last month, concluded nursing student did nothing

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so the next piece goes inside
excluding means the letters for the month are taken out

parts.note: to have decided is to have concluded
December, the last month of the year, is abbreviated Dec
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Apart from last month, a student on a nursing course was idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' looks like a profession but means holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be idle is to laze about without working, the past tense matching did nothing.

clue.text: Bury doctor model briefly introduces

indicators.note: introduces means the shortened model comes in front of the doctor
briefly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a toy is a small model
MB is the medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, held by a doctor

explanation.surface: A model briefly introduces a doctor, who is then told to bury something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' is a verb, and the answer can be one too, meaning to entomb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to place a body in a burial vault or grave is to inter it.

clue.text: I go off cycling as complete beginner

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved round from one end to the other

parts.note: to rot is to go off, as food does

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a bike as a complete novice.
explanation.walkthrough: IROT has its last letter cycled round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or new recruit, from the Latin for a young soldier.

clue.text: Stealthy criminal using a knife he's ground over time

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters cover the next piece
ground as in crushed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar wields a knife he has spent a long time sharpening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges A KNIFE HE'S, and 'over' wraps those letters round T. 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who steals furtively without breaking in, sneaking into unlocked premises.

clue.text: Slimming and fasting, say, mixing new drugs to lose weight

indicators.note: mixing says these letters are rearranged
to lose means a letter is dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: Diets and fasts, along with new drugs, help people lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose weight' removes W from NEWDRUGS, and 'mixing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb forms ending in -ing used as nouns, like slimming and fasting, are examples of this grammar term.

clue.text: Shopkeepers receiving note for latest in legal fees

indicators.note: receiving says the shopkeepers take in a new letter
for means one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: retailers are shopkeepers

indicators.note: latest in means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers get a note about the latest legal charges.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'legal' is replaced by N; 'legal' serves the wordplay, leaving 'fees' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fees paid in advance to secure a barrister's or lawyer's services are given this name.

clue.text: Challenge firm refusal to withdraw court claims

indicators.note: claims means holds, so the court abbreviation goes round the next piece
to withdraw means to pull back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: set means firm, as jelly sets
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A company's flat refusal to drop its legal claims is challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: SETNO is reversed to ONTES by 'to withdraw', and 'claims' puts it inside CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or oppose something, as with a will or a decision, is to challenge it.

clue.text: Entertaining article about looker read out secretly

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the outer pieces take in the next one

parts.note: on means about or concerning

indicators.note: read out signals a word that is spoken, its sound giving the letters

parts.note: a looker is an attractive person, a cutie
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A fun piece about someone attractive is read out in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like an adjective for the article, but it means hosting.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom, from 'quiet', meaning on the quiet or covertly.

clue.text: Ends having word with elected politicians from the centre

parts.note: a term is a word
in means elected, as a party gets in

indicators.note: from the centre means the middle letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Talks with elected politicians of the centre come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'with' are link words; the middle letter of 'politicians' is I.
explanation.definitionFit: End stations of rail or bus lines, or end points generally, plural to match ends.

clue.text: Mild expletive criticised

definitions.meaning: a gentle curse such as 'drat' or 'damned', said in annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone swears mildly at being criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a softened oath like 'darned' and a verb meaning slammed or lambasted.

clue.text: Nurse typically that in conversation displays charm

indicators.note: in conversation means the words are heard spoken

parts.note: a nurse bee is a typical bee, followed by which, meaning that

explanation.surface: A nurse in conversation shows charm towards patients.
explanation.walkthrough: A nurse bee tends larvae in a hive, so a nurse is typically a bee; BEE WHICH said aloud gives the answer. 'displays' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or captivate someone is to cast a charm over them.

clue.text: Spirit shown by writer after switching focus

indicators.note: switching focus means the two central letters trade places

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: An author shows spirit after changing his focus.
explanation.walkthrough: A Biro is the British name for a ballpoint pen; swapping its middle letters I and R gives the answer. 'shown by' and 'after' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour or liveliness, as in playing with great zest, is a synonym for spirit.

clue.text: Boast of attendance United ultimately rejected

indicators.note: rejected means that letter is thrown out

parts.note: a crowd is the attendance at a match

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Boasting about the attendance figures, United were ultimately rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'United', D, is removed from CROWD; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag or gloat loudly is a verb synonymous with boast.

clue.text: Churchill paintings, possibly seen back in March

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: Churchill was a Prime Minister, PM
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: Winston Churchill's paintings might have been shown again in March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is a verb here, not the month; 'seen' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with heavy steps over a long way is to march or trudge.

clue.text: Queue I'd anticipated turning up, around so long

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
around means the clue words lie round the answer, which is concealed within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A queue someone expected forms, and they say goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'around so long' as the definition, but 'around' is the hidden-word signal: the words lie around the answer. The definition is 'so long' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived farewell, used in English to say goodbye.

clue.text: Live with facial hair for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a beard is facial hair

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates facial hair, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or put up with something is to live with it.

clue.text: Nothing wrong? We're told I will make a bloomer

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
X is the mark for a wrong answer

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE

explanation.surface: Someone denies anything is wrong but admits they will make a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' means a flower here, not a mistake; the pronoun I spoken sounds like EYE. 'will make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a flowering plant, and a flower is a crossword bloomer.

clue.text: Air view occasionally on indigenous Canadian tackling tango, untaught

indicators.note: on means placed after, in an across clue
tackling means taking on, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: an Inuit is a member of an indigenous people of northern Canada
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An Inuit dancer takes on the tango with natural flair, never taught.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'Air view' give IVE, placed after INTUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing something instinctively, without being taught, is to be intuitive.

clue.text: Five clubs maybe immediately having plenty of money

parts.note: straight means immediately, as in 'straight away'
flush means rich, having plenty of money

explanation.surface: Five golf clubs might be bought at once by someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' is the card suit: five consecutive cards of one suit form this poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, five cards in sequence of one suit, such as clubs, make this hand.
